title: I Sing My Saviour's Wondrous Death
description: I Sing My Saviour's Wondrous Death in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 114, headed “Christ's death, victory and dominion”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I sing my Sav-iour's won-drous death; He con-quer'd when he fell: 'Tis fin-ish'd, said his dy-ing breath, And shook the gates of hell.

lines: I sing my Saviour's wondrous death;
And shook the gates of hell.
Hence shall his sovereign throne arise,
His cross a sure foundation laid
When thro' the regions of the dead
He pass'd to reach the crown.
To heaven and hell his hands divide
The saints from his propitious eye
And all the sons of darkness fly

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
